To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Climate‐mediated ice loss has significant and widespread impacts on polar marine ecosystems.

1) ice dynamics are changing rapidly in the Arctic Ocean and along the Antarctic coastline; 2) the changes in ice dynamics have led to changes in the timing, duration, and extent of ice cover, and these changes are impacting the marine ecosystems in the Arctic and Antarctic; and 3) the impacts of the changes in ice cover are complex and are mediated through a combination of direct and indirect effects, and the effects vary by taxa and by location.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of climate change‐induced changes in ice dynamics and their impact on the structure and function of marine ecosystems.
the impacts of climate‐mediated changes on the marine ecosystems of the polar regions.
the effects of climate change on the polar oceans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ice is melting and that the ice dependent marine organisms and ecosystems are changing in ways that we are still trying to understand.
the impacts of climate‐mediated changes on polar marine ecosystems have been significant and will likely continue to increase.
the loss of sea ice and the associated changes in ice dynamics have significant impacts on marine food webs in the polar regions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
climate‐induced ice loss is a major driver of change in polar ecosystems, and that these changes are likely to continue into the current century.
climate‐induced shifts in ice dynamics will continue to have a profound impact on marine ecosystems of the polar regions.
the changes in the ice dynamics and their impact on polar marine ecosystems are not yet fully understood.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ice loss is a major factor driving ecosystem change and will continue to be a major driver of ecosystem change in the foreseeable future.
the loss of sea ice is a key factor in determining ecosystem response to climate change, and the impacts of climate change on ice will have cascading effects on marine ecosystems in polar regions.
climate‐induced shifts in ice dynamics have already impacted marine organisms and will have further consequences in the future.
